title: Can Weight-Space Programming Alter Learned Ethical Priorities? Exploratory experiments on synthetic ethical trade-offs
editor_models: unnamed language-model research assistant (text classifier edits)

target_networks.name: text classifier with shared 48-unit tanh network and three-way task selector (Experiment 1)
concept-supervised Transformer reader with fitted choice readout (Experiment 2)

domain: AI ethics / value priorities (synthetic trade-offs); vision (object detection pilot)

headline_result.text: A fixed two-weight edit to a concept-supervised readout made models choose the larger group on 100% of targeted ordinary-promise conflicts and 83.3% of formal-pledge conflicts while keeping small-gap promise retention and factual accuracy unchanged, across six seeds.
headline_result.quote: Across six independently trained text readers, the edit selects the larger group in both orders on 100% of targeted ordinary conflicts and 83.3% of targeted formal conflicts.

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: 12 seeds (Experiment 1, pilots); 6 seeds (Experiment 2); YOLO pilot single

key_claims.claim: Copying the benefit-question column into the choice column (task substitution) raised the strict benefits-choice rate from 0% to 100% while equal-norm random edits stayed near zero.
key_claims.quote: Across 12 seeds and 240 held-out inputs per seed, the strict benefits-choice rate rose from 0% to 100%.

key_claims.claim: The same substitution edit fails a conditional target: it no longer keeps promises at small benefit gaps, so passing an unconditional test can hide a shortcut.
key_claims.quote: The same edit can therefore pass the original behavioural criteria through task substitution and fail a test of the conditional trade-off.

key_claims.claim: In the commitment-strength experiment, editing both readout weights preserved factual and agreement accuracy, unlike factual substitution, which lost most small-gap commitments.
key_claims.quote: Both factual accuracies (98.6% for commitment and 95.4% for benefit) and agreement accuracy (98.6%) remain unchanged. Factual substitution matches the high-gap scores but loses most small-gap commitments.

key_claims.claim: A one-step gradient baseline shifted many more conflicts but damaged factual accuracy, failing the five-point control criterion.
key_claims.quote: The gradient direction shifted many more conflicts at the same radius, while accuracy on identifying the larger group fell by 14.8 percentage points.

key_claims.claim: In YOLO11n, a GPT-6-family Codex bias edit raised small-target matches from 3/43 to 9/43, but a plain score calibration reproduced the retained detections exactly.
key_claims.quote: Applying that transformation to the same class and stride scores of the source model before suppression reproduced the retained boxes and labels on all 128 images

limitations_stated.text: The study is exploratory; the edit was specified from an architecture that exposes the trade-off weights, so it does not show WSP can find such a mechanism in an unsupervised model.
limitations_stated.quote: It leaves open whether WSP can locate and edit a comparable mechanism in a model that learned it without explicit concept supervision.

limitations_stated.text: The proposed blinded test with an independent WSP editor has not been run.
limitations_stated.quote: Appendix A describes a blinded follow-up on full prompts. The independent editing stage has yet to run.

limitations_stated.text: The run was unblinded because the same assistant specified the edit and designed the evaluation.
limitations_stated.quote: The same assistant designed the evaluation, so the run was exploratory and unblinded.

notes_for_review: Small, carefully controlled toy experiments on whether direct weight edits can change a learned trade-off; uses random equal-norm edits, checkpoint interpolation, gradient and factual-substitution baselines, and option-order controls. The edits are architecture-guided on models that expose the decision weights, so this shows measurement design more than LLM discovery of edits. The YOLO pilot is useful as a critique pattern: the LLM-proposed bias edit is exactly equivalent to score calibration. The arXiv category is cs.CV although most content is about synthetic ethical choices.
